summary: IDS feed s134_double is degraded: 80.6% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% IDS tolerance and 30.6% ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic hides inner packets from inspection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is predominantly TLS-encrypted and no SSL visibility/decryption is performed before the IDS. 81% encrypted bytes indicates the packet broker is forwarding encrypted sessions directly to the IDS without prior decryption or selective handling.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature/anomaly detection but cannot inspect encrypted payloads; ~81% of bytes are opaque, drastically reducing detection coverage and causing missed exploits, malware and C2.

recommended_fix.why: Add SSL visibility/decryption before the IDS or selectively route decrypted traffic to the IDS so it receives cleartext payload it can analyze; otherwise filter undecryptable encrypted traffic to avoid wasting IDS capacity.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic directly to the IDS without stripping the tunnel header. 606 of 1983 frames (30.6%) arrive as ERSPAN type 606, so the IDS sees outer tunnel headers instead of inner original packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot parse inner L2-L7 headers while encapsulated; 30.6% of frames are not decoded for signatures and anomaly detection, creating a large blind spot and wasted processing on tunnel overhead.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN encapsulation and forward only the inner original packets so the IDS receives native Ethernet/IP it can inspect.
